principles: Single source of truth: extract autoCommitStoryMetadata into a shared helper rather than duplicate the git add+commit logic per handler
Path-scoped staging: git add .koala/story/actives/<id>/ is the safety boundary; classifier is belt-and-suspenders for the tail-note hint not for blocking
Idempotent: re-running the helper when nothing is staged returns empty string and does nothing — safe to call after every metadata write
drivers: B-c9f5 dirty gate loop where koala metadata writes from REVIEW/TEST commands kept showing as koala_metadata_changes between gate runs
story_advance already proves the auto-commit pattern works (used since B-6326 lifecycle); B-3506 just extends the coverage
Without coverage, B-4b22 (Material Dirty Gate Policy) cannot tighten the policy because koala_metadata_changes would still be common — extending auto-commit makes that category trend to empty

options.name: A: Extract auto-commit helper to core/ and call from each metadata-writing handler
pros: Centralized git logic in one place
Each handler explicitly opts in with a reason string (clear intent at call site)
Easy to audit which handlers do/dont auto-commit
Tail-note about coexisting non-metadata dirt is one-line addition reusing classifier
cons: Touches 6-8 handler files to add the call
Each handler has to import the helper and pass storyId + reason

options.name: B: Hook auto-commit at store.write* layer
pros: One change covers all current and future writers
cons: store.ts is currently pure data layer (no git side-effects); breaking that invariant invites surprises
Hard to attribute commits to the operation that caused them (no reason string)
Some writers (e.g. process-metrics.json) intentionally batch — they would now produce one commit per write

options.name: C: Wrap every CLI command at registry level with a post-success commit
cons: Cannot tell which commands wrote metadata vs which were read-only; would auto-commit nothing on read-only commands or spurious commits otherwise
Reason string is the command name not the semantic operation
Would commit at command boundary not write boundary, missing multi-step handlers

chosen: A: Extract auto-commit helper to core/ and call from each metadata-writing handler
rationale: Choose A because explicit per-handler opt-in is the right granularity: each handler has clear semantics about what it wrote and why, and the call site documents the auto-commit reason for audit. Reject B because store.ts is the project's pure data layer per CLAUDE.md design (Data/Machine/Fn separation) and pushing git side-effects there violates the invariant the codebase already follows. Reject C because command-level wrapping cannot distinguish metadata-writing from read-only operations and would either generate spurious commits or miss multi-step handlers. The 6-8 handler edits in A are mostly identical one-line additions reading the helper output and concatenating into the response — low cognitive cost.

preMortem.scenario: Helper accidentally bundles a material/fixture/unexpected file because storyDirRel gets refactored to a broader path
preMortem.trigger: Future change broadens store.storyDirRel() return value, or a developer copy-pastes the helper but changes the path argument
preMortem.consequence: Auto-commit silently includes a partially-edited source file alongside metadata, masking material drift from gate checks
preMortem.mitigation: Helper accepts only the literal pathPattern .koala/story/actives/<id>/ (computed inside the helper from storyId, not passed by caller) and asserts at runtime that storyDirRel starts with the canonical prefix; reject otherwise. Smoke test covers: refactor that broadens the prefix → helper throws.

preMortem.scenario: Auto-commit fires recursively when koala validate / session_brief itself calls a metadata-writing handler
preMortem.trigger: validate handler writes test-evidence.json then calls finding_add internally; both would try to commit
preMortem.consequence: Multiple commits per command, polluting git log
preMortem.mitigation: Helper is idempotent — re-run when nothing is staged is no-op (returns empty hint). Multiple call sites within one command still produce at most one commit because the second call finds nothing to stage. Smoke test: handler A calls handler B; both invoke helper; only one commit in git log.

preMortem.scenario: User sees coexisting non-metadata dirt note but assumes auto-commit handled it
preMortem.trigger: Helper prints tail-note about coexisting dirt; user reads it as confirmation that everything is committed
preMortem.consequence: User advances to TEST/DONE thinking dirt is clean, but material file still blocks
preMortem.mitigation: Tail-note wording is unambiguous: must read like (coexisting non-metadata dirt left untouched: material_source_changes=2, fixture_changes=1, unexpected_dirty_files=1). The word untouched is the anchor. Smoke test asserts the exact string left untouched appears and user-visible output never says all clean or fully committed when non-metadata dirt is present.
